newsitem.title: CANADA: BASEBALL-CLEMENS THROWS SHUTOUT FOR 17TH WIN AS JAYS BEAT TRIBE.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-CLEMENS THROWS SHUTOUT FOR 17TH WIN AS JAYS BEAT TRIBE.

text.p: Roger Clemens fired a five-hitter for his 40th career shutout and became the first 17-game winner in the majors as the Toronto Blue Jays beat the Cleveland Indians 4-0 Thursday for their third straight win.
Clemens (17-4) walked three and struck out 10 in his seventh complete game of the season. He also notched his 199th strikeout of the season, passing Dave Stieb for the franchise record.

"Those things are special, those little side notes, but the game's the bottom line," Clemens said. "The crowd was great tonight, I credit them with helping me get stronger. When they're cheering like that for you, you can't help but get excited about what you're doing out there and reach back for a little extra."
Clemens lowered his major league-leading earned run average to 1.69.
"He's really been that way all year," said catcher Charlie O'Brien. "He's done an outstanding job day in, day out, every time out almost."

"He pitched tough," Cleveland's Brian Giles said. "Every time he goes out there you know you're going to have to go up there and battle. I thought we swung the bats pretty well. I thought we hit some balls pretty hard, but we just didn't have any placement tonight. We couldn't hang with him."
Cleveland starter John Smiley (1-1) took the loss.

"Roger pitched a great game, he had it going on tonight," Smiley said. "With Roger out on the hill and the year he's having, you can't afford to give up any runs. We got a few hits off him, he got some key double plays. We hit some balls right at people."
Cleveland concluded a 3-4 road trip, but kept a 3 1/2-game lead over second-place Milwaukee in the American League Central.
In Seattle, Mike Blowers and Ken Griffey Jr accounted for two homers and all three Seattle hits, helping Jeff Fassero record his third straight win as the Mariners edged the Chicago White Sox, 3-2.
Griffey hit his 34th homer of the year in the fifth after doubling in the third.

Fassero (11-6) went 7 1/3 innings, giving up a run and four hits. Mike Timlin and Norm Charlton combined for one inning before Heathcliff Slocumb got the final two outs for his 19th save and second with the Mariners.
Rookie Scott Eyre (0-2) allowed all three runs and three hits in five innings, but issued six walks. The White Sox walked eight.
Frank Thomas hit his 26th homer for Chicago, which has lost nine of its last 12 games.

At Texas, David Cone allowed two runs over seven innings and Bernie Williams had three hits, including a two-run homer, to lead the New York Yankees to their eighth victory in 10 games, 4-2 over the Rangers.

Cone (12-5) yielded three hits with two walks and eight strikeouts and has held opponents to three runs or less in his last six appearances. Mariano Rivera survived a shaky ninth to record his major league-leading 34th save.
Texas starter Bobby Witt (10-9) surrendered four runs and nine hits over 6 1/3 innnings.

In Kansas City, Glenn Dishman struck out a career-high eight in seven innings for his first major-league win in nearly two years and Bob Hamelin burned his former team with a homer and an RBI double as the Detroit Tigers beat the Royals 8-4.
Bob Higginson and Damion Easley also homered for Detroit while Joe Vitiello, Chili Davis and Jeff King had solo shots for Kansas City.
Dishman (1-0), whose last win came for the Padres at St. Louis in August 1995, captured his first American League victory by allowing two runs and six hits with one walk.
The Tigers won their 53rd game of the season, matching their total from all of last year.
Tim Belcher (11-10) had his personal three-game winning streak halted, allowing all eight runs and 11 hits.

At Minnesota, Mike Benjamin's RBI triple highlighted a five-run second inning and Aaron Sele won for the first time in more than a month as the surging Boston Red Sox edged the Twins 7-6 for their fourth straight win.
Boston took three of five games in Minnesota this season. It marked the first time since 1989 that the Red Sox have won the season series in Minneapolis.

Sele (11-8) snapped a five-start winless streak and won for the first time since July 3. In 5 1/3 rocky innings he allowed six runs -- four earned -- and four hits, walking four and striking out four.
In Oakland, Rafael Bournigal's one-out single in the bottom of the 13th scored Ernie Young as the Athletics posted consecutive wins for the first time in three weeks, 5-4 over the Milwaukee Brewers.

Bournigal also knocked in the go-ahead run in Wednesday's victory over the White Sox. The Athletics, who lost nine of their previous 11 games, had not posted back-to-back wins since a three-game winning streak from July 15-17.
